title: Midnight
logline: At half past ten Bhaiyaji phones his 'Inspector sahab' and invites him to the godown at midnight, alone, to stamp the slip for eight hundred sacks of ration grain. Pushpa brings news that the SHO's call to Bhaiyaji connected that evening. The DSP refuses a raid, orders Nirala locked up now and says any officer who helps him will be named in the same FIR. Nirala lays a carved teak revolver on the desk and holds out his wrists, and Nandini has to choose.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; names, 'madam', 'sahab', 'ji', 'thana', 'godown', 'FIR' and 'lockup' kept as spoken in India.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, six weeks into her first posting at the Imlipur thana. Tonight she is in the fake thana with its 'Inspector', with his files and with an order to have him in her lockup before ten tomorrow.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves buttoned at the wrist; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars each; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip; black shoes; blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no name tag, no stars. Her cherry-red open-face scooter helmet sits on the complainants' bench all episode.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral educated small-city north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Quick and clipped. Under pressure she gets quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic. Tonight she is under pressure from b6 on: every line after that is lower and more exact than the one before.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: The self-appointed 'Inspector' of the fake thana in the shut Roopam Talkies. To Bhaiyaji he is 'Inspector sahab'; to Nandini and Pushpa, 'Nirala ji'.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, a neat black pencil moustache, clean-shaven chin. A home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams drooping past his shoulders, sleeves to his knuckles, collar standing away from his neck, trousers belted high with the belt tail hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES: khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge, worn dead level. One large home-made medal above his left chest pocket: a blank brass-yellow disc as wide as his palm on a broad maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon. Brown leather holster with a buttoned flap on his right hip, holding the wooden revolver until b8.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned small-town north-Indian English, as learnt from manuals, with a clear Hindi accent; not British, not American. No contractions tonight ('It is', 'I am', 'I will'). English police terms pronounced with great care. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes. Under pressure he becomes more formal and quieter and his sentences get shorter. Frightened is a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. Tonight he is frightened from b1 on; play b8 and b9 straight, with no comic colour at all.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable at the Imlipur thana for twenty-six years. She heard part of the SHO's call to Bhaiyaji at seven and has walked across the line to say so.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid, round shoulders. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low on her nose. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar on each teal epaulette, lantern sleeve patches, under an open hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan with two sagging pockets, a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. A cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried small-town north-Indian English with a clear Hindi accent; not British, not American. Short sentences; says the important thing in the fewest words. Keeps 'madam' and 'SHO sahab'. Never surprised. Tonight she arrives out of breath from the walk, but the facts come out level and exact.

characters.name: Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur
characters.role: Runs the ration godown and most of Imlipur. Voice only in this episode, on Nirala's keypad phone, on speaker.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice. Soft, hospitable small-town north-Indian English with a strong Hindi accent; not British, not American. Keeps 'Inspector sahab'. Courteous to the point of menace; never threatens, never hurries, laughs before he says the worst thing. Tonight he sounds ordinary and friendly: the invitation must sound like every other month. Heard through the small speaker of a keypad phone in the mix (narrow band), filter wide enough that consonants survive.

characters.name: Anil Rathore, DSP
characters.role: The sub-division's DSP. Holds a press conference at the Imlipur thana at ten tomorrow. Voice only in this episode, on Nandini's phone.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone; a man always half addressing the press. Fluent, brisk officer's Indian English, city-educated north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Says 'SI Joshi'. Impatient, gives orders as times and places. Phone-filtered in the mix and must stay fully intelligible, above all l17. Never shouts: the last line is level and final.

location: talkies_lobby: the lobby of the shut Roopam Talkies, fitted out as a police station. Terrazzo floor, two round pillars, empty film-poster frames (painted blank). Centre: Nirala's desk, the old booking counter, with registers squared in a stack, the red-cloth thick file, a rubber stamp, a tin ink pad, a kettle and two glasses, and Nirala's small keypad phone lying face up. Behind the desk the hand-painted board (painted blank; overlay ov_fake_board). To one side the complainants' bench, with Nandini's red helmet on it; to the other the ticket-booth lockup with its arched grille window. A wall clock with hands and no numerals. One bare bulb over the desk; the lobby doors open on the dark, and far off through them the red railway signal lamp at the crossing.
time_of_day: Night, about 10:30 p.m. to 11 p.m. One bare bulb; everything outside its circle is dark.

beats.action: OPEN ON A SOUND, no establishing shot. Black for a breath, then the buzz. Shot 1 (insert, top-down): Nirala's keypad phone face up on the desk under the bulb, rattling on the wood, its little screen lit (overlay ov_caller_bhaiyaji). Shot 2 (two-shot across the desk): Nirala in his cap behind the counter, his hands flat either side of the phone; Nandini standing opposite, picture-left. Both are looking down at the phone. l01 plays here. Shot 3 (single): Nandini looks up at him for l02. Silence: 1.5 s of buzzing before l01.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] Bhaiyaji.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Pick up. On speaker.

beats.action: Bhaiyaji's voice fills the lobby, warm and ordinary, from the small phone speaker. Four stills. Shot 1 (insert, close): the phone on the desk, screen lit, Nirala's finger just lifting off the key (l03). Shot 2 (insert): Nirala's hands flat on the desk, sleeves over his knuckles (l04). Shot 3 (insert, close): the rubber stamp and tin ink pad by his sleeve, so the picture lands on 'stamp' (l05). Shot 4 (single, close): Nandini listening, eyes on the phone, very still (l06). Bhaiyaji is never seen.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [chuckles] Inspector sahab! Tonight at twelve, come to the godown.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] Eight hundred sacks are going out.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] The crossing is under your outpost. The slip needs your stamp.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [chuckles] As always. [quietly] Do come alone.

beats.action: The call ends: a click and the end-of-call tones, then only the bulb's hum. Shot 1 (two-shot across the desk, same set-up as b1 shot 2): the phone screen has gone dark; Nirala gives it one small nod, the nod of a man who takes this call every month. Hold in silence (1.2 s). Shot 2 (single, Nandini): she looks from the phone to the red-cloth file on the desk and says what tonight is. Low, not excited.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Eight hundred sacks. The town's ration. Red-handed.

beats.action: Shot 1 (wide from behind the desk): Pushpa in the open lobby doorway, out of the dark, out of breath, the knitting bag swinging on her left shoulder; she has walked across the line. 1.0 s of footsteps and breath before l08. Shot 2 (two-shot, Pushpa and Nandini at the desk's end; Nirala only as sleeves and hands at the frame edge): l08. Shot 3 (single, Pushpa, level, spectacles low): l09. Shot 4 (single, Nandini, sharp): l10. Shot 5 (second framing of shot 3 at a scale of 1.3 or less): l11. No more than two faces in any frame.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [sighs] Madam. This evening SHO sahab phoned Bhaiyaji. It went through.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] I heard the word 'talkies'. Then the door shut.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] What did Bhaiyaji say?

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] Nobody heard that part.

beats.action: Shot 1 (insert, top-down, held in silence 1.5 s): the dark keypad phone on the desk, and around it three sets of hands: Nirala's, sleeves over the knuckles; Nandini's, flat; Pushpa's, holding the working pair of needles from her knitting bag (the two in her bun stay in), still. No faces. Shot 2 (single, Nirala, close, cap level under the bulb): he states the problem like a clerk reading a register; his voice is thinner than before. The pause on the ellipsis is real.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] Call in the evening. Invitation at night. And the words... the same as every month.

beats.action: Nandini tries the lawful road on her own black phone. She has stepped away to a pillar, phone at her right ear; we join the call after she has asked for a raid. The DSP is voice only, through the phone. Shot 1 (single, at the pillar, phone at her right ear; 1.0 s silent): l13. Shot 2 (second framing of shot 1 at a scale of 1.3 or less, tighter on her face): l14. Shot 3 (insert, top-down): Nirala's dark keypad phone on the desk, the phone the DSP is dismissing: l15. Shot 4 (insert at the desk): Nirala's hands gone still on the counter and, beside them, Pushpa's working needles from her knitting bag stopped in the orange wool: l16. Shot 5 (single, close on Nandini's face): she hears the price; l17 plays over it, and the frame holds on her after the line ends.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [sharply] Whose information is this?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] I heard Bhaiyaji's own voice, DSP sir. On Nirala's phone.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [calm] We don't raid on what's heard over a fake thana's phone, SI Joshi.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [sharply] Put him in the lockup. Now.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [calm] Any officer who helps him will be named in the same FIR.

beats.action: The call is over. 0.8 s silent: she lowers the phone. She says both roads aloud, to Pushpa, flatly, one image for each. Shot 1 (insert): the empty ticket-booth lockup, its arched grille window dark: l18. Shot 2 (two-shot, Nandini and Pushpa by the pillar, Nandini picture-left): l19. Shot 3 (through the open lobby doors): the red railway signal lamp, small, far off in the dark: the first sentence of l20, 'If I let him go, only he can get inside.'. Shot 4 (second framing of shot 2 at a scale of 1.3 or less, on Nandini): the rest of l20, 'On my word. Against orders.'; the distant horn follows the line. The picture cut sits on l20's first full stop, and the l20 subtitle cue splits there (D-014 rules 3 and 7).

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] If I arrest him now, he's in my lockup. Alive.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] But then the SHO stamps the slip, and I can't stop a truck with his stamp.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] If I let him go, only he can get inside. On my word. Against orders.

beats.action: PLAYED STRAIGHT: no joke, no comic tag, no music sting. Shot 1 (two-shot across the desk, Nandini picture-left, Nirala picture-right): her eyes on the holster at his right hip; l21. Then 1.5 s silent while he unbuttons the flap and lays the revolver down. Shot 2 (insert, close, in profile under the bulb): the revolver lying on its side on the desk, pale teak, the grain and a knot visible, no metal anywhere, pointing at neither of them and not at the camera; his fingers just leaving it: l22. Shot 3 (insert): his hand hovering over it, not steady: l23. Shot 4 (single, Nirala, cap level, eyes down at the wood): l24.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] You have a revolver.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] It is wood, madam. Teak. I carved it myself.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] In two years it has never left the holster.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] He has a real one.

beats.action: Frightened, formal, steady. 1.0 s silent: he holds out both wrists across the desk, side by side, sleeves over his knuckles, the wooden revolver on the desk just behind them. Shot 1 (single, Nirala, front on, cap dead level): l25. Shot 2 (insert): the two outstretched wrists over the desk, from Nandini's side: l26, which he leaves unfinished.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] I am not police, madam. You are.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [quietly] If you tell me to, I will go. If you tell me to...

beats.action: ENDING, SPOKEN: THE QUESTION. Shot 1 (one held frame, 1.0 s silent before the line): his two wrists low in frame; above them Nandini's right hand holding the open handcuffs, just taken from the pouch on her right hip; the wooden revolver on the desk between. Shot 2 (single, Nandini, front on, under the bulb; the wall clock behind her, hour hand on eleven, minute hand on twelve): she asks it aloud, low and clear, to no one. Pushpa is in the room, out of frame. Hold 1.5 s after the line. The stage keeps this frame (shot 2) for the question card.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] Do I cuff him, or let him be Inspector tonight?

sfx_notes: Bed, whole episode, loopable (one talkies_lobby night ambience for the series): the hum of one bare bulb, crickets outside the open lobby doors, a slow wall-clock tick. Nothing in it is loud.

b1: an old keypad phone on silent-vibrate, rattling hard on a wooden counter; it starts on black, before the first picture, and runs 1.5 s before l01, then stops dead under l01. Shared series effect: make it once.

b2: a soft key click as he presses speaker, then Bhaiyaji through a small phone loudspeaker (narrow band, a little room echo off the terrazzo). Keep the filter wide enough that consonants survive. Bed down under l03 to l06.
b3: after l06, a click and three short end-of-call tones; then only the bulb hum for the 1.2 s hold.
b4: quick footsteps on terrazzo coming in from the dark, the knitting bag's soft thump, Pushpa's breath under l08. The breath dies away before l09.
b5: 1.5 s of near-silence: bulb hum, clock tick, one far dog bark. No music.

b6: the DSP through a phone filter at her ear (narrower than Bhaiyaji's speaker, still intelligible). Nothing loud anywhere in b6: no train, no door. The bed ducks further under l17 so every word of it is clear.
b7: after the last word of l20, and only then, a distant goods-train horn, low and far, fading under b8 shot 1 and l21 (b8 opens on l21; its 1.5 s silence comes after l21).
b8: in the 1.5 s silence, the leather flap unbuttoning and a light hollow knock of wood laid on wood. Not a metallic sound. Nothing else.
b10: in the silence before l27, one dry metallic click of the handcuffs opening; it must be over before the line starts. The bed ducks right down under l27 and stays down through the 1.5 s hold.
music_note: No music for b1 to b5: phone, bulb and crickets only. From b6 a single low sustained string note, barely audible, enters under the DSP call and ducks under l17. It drops out completely for b8 (the revolver is played straight, with no sting). Under b10 one soft sustained note returns, ducked under l27, and is cut to silence at the end of the hold so the question card lands in silence. Instrumental, no melody, no percussion hits.
ending_question: Will Nandini keep a frightened, unarmed man safe in her lockup and let eight hundred sacks go out on the SHO's stamp, or send him, against her own DSP's order, to a Bhaiyaji who may already know everything?
writer_notes: English adaptation of script.hi.json (revision 1), not a literal translation. Same beats (b1 to b10), same speakers, same line ids (l01 to l27) in the same order, same emotion tags in the same positions, same silent_seconds per beat. Only text, target_seconds, the English names and voice notes, and the three places where action quotes spoken words differ. Sources: content/series2/bible.json (character language.en registers, choice.question.en, episode title), docs/decisions.md D-004, D-006 (change 19: 'The English is unchanged'), D-008, D-013, D-014, D-016 and the Gate 0b entries D-0M2 to D-0M4.

The cliffhanger l27 is the bible's locked English question, word for word: 'Do I cuff him, or let him be Inspector tonight?' (choice.question.en). 'Him' stands in for the Hindi 'इन्हें'; she says 'he' of him in l18 and l20 just as the Hindi says 'ये' and 'यही'.

Registers, from the bible's language.en entries: Nandini neutral and clipped, with 'DSP sir' on the phone and 'the SHO' of Tripathi; Nirala manual-taught English with no contractions ('It is wood', 'I am not police', 'I will go'), his l12 kept as clipped register entries like the Hindi; Pushpa short and plain, keeping 'madam' and 'SHO sahab'; Bhaiyaji soft and hospitable, keeping 'Inspector sahab', with the courteous 'Do come alone' for 'अकेले आइएगा'; the DSP brisk, with contractions and 'SI Joshi'. Nobody says a bare 'sahab' or 'sir' about a third party (D-004 direction 5).

One word per object, matching the Hindi choices: 'stamp' for मोहर (l05, l19; b2 shot 3 now lands on 'stamp'), 'slip', 'godown', 'truck', 'lockup', 'outpost' for चौकी (the overlay's English is 'Police Outpost Imlipur'), 'sacks' for बोरी, 'cuff' only in the question. l07 keeps D-016 direction 1: 'The town's ration.'

Action text: b2, b7 and nothing else were changed, and only where they quote spoken words ('stamp' for 'मोहर'; the English halves of l20 and 'first full stop' for 'first ।'). Picture, shot order, on_screen, location, sfx_notes and music_note are unchanged, because both language cuts share frames and sound. The b7 picture cut and subtitle split sit after 'only he can get inside.'

Length, counted by hand (no shell in this session): about 1,168 characters of English dialogue (1,160 before the english_review change to l26), without tags, the space after a tag, or speaker labels. Targets assume about 11.5 characters a second for ordinary lines and about 10.5 for [quietly] lines, plus about 0.4 s for each [chuckles] or [sighs] and about 0.2 s per internal full stop. That is slower than the proof's English targets (about 13 a second), because the photoreal English cut measured 35.9 s against 31.7 s planned (D-0M4) and v4 takes ran 20 to 60 per cent over target (D-0M2). Lines were not padded to match the Hindi.

Running time: spoken targets 108.1 s, 13 speaker changes at 0.3 s (3.9 s), silences 12.0 s: 124.0 s (was 107.4 s and 123.3 s before l26 went from 4.2 to 4.9 s in the english_review), against 132.8 s for the Hindi. Each language's timeline is built from its own measured clips (D-014 rule 6), so the English running shorter needs no fix; shots follow the voice.

Lines more than about 15 per cent shorter than their Hindi target, so their stills will run shorter in the English cut (no padding added, per the brief): l06 (3.0 against 3.8), l11 (2.0 against 2.4), l18 (4.2 against 5.8), l21 (2.0 against 2.4), l22 (4.2 against 5.0), l24 (1.8 against 2.2), l25 (3.0 against 3.8), l27 (4.6 against 5.8). Two lines run over their Hindi target: l12 (7.6 against 7.0, about 9 per cent) and l26 (4.9 against 4.2, about 17 per cent, just past the 15 per cent guide; accepted in the english_review because 'If you tell me to' is the natural English for 'आप कहें तो', and b9 shot 2 is an insert that simply holds 0.7 s longer). b8 shot 4 (l24, about 1.8 s) and b1 shot 2 (l01, about 1.2 s) are the shortest stills; if the editor wants a floor, hold the frame past the line rather than adding words.

Silences and where they sit (same as the Hindi): b1 before l01; b3 before l07; b4 before l08; b5 before l12; b6 before l13; b7 before l18; b8 between l21 and l22 (the revolver is laid down); b9 before l25; b10 1.0 s before l27 and 1.5 s after it.

Tags: every Hindi tag kept on the same line and in the same position, since each still fits the English read. [flatly] on l18 is in the verify group; if the nandini voice ignores it, swap to [calm]. The review note's option to change l03 to [calm] (two [chuckles] in four Bhaiyaji lines) is left to S10, as in the Hindi. No tag is followed by an ellipsis; no line is a true whisper; l27 is [quietly], low and fully voiced, with the bed ducked under it.

Extra takes: l01 'Bhaiyaji.' is a one-word turn; flag for extra takes, fallback text 'It is Bhaiyaji, madam.'. l24 'He has a real one.' is short and nervous; flag alongside it. 'SI Joshi' (l15) may be read as the word 'sigh': flag for extra takes and add it to the pronunciation dictionary as the letters S-I.

Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Bhaiyaji (BHAI-yaa-jee), sahab (SAA-hab), thana (THAA-naa), Nirala (ni-RAA-laa), Joshi (JOH-shee), godown (go-DOWN, as said in India), talkies (TAW-keez), SI, SHO, DSP and FIR as letters.

The ending question is not answered by any spoken line: the last line is the choice itself, and what Bhaiyaji knows is still unknown on screen. Neither the transfer application nor the slip's existing stamp is mentioned (bible balance_rules). No recap, no narrator.
